delay(Delay::dlx_ttl()) makes retry_after wait on the broker: the copy parks in a waiting queue under a per-message TTL. On a retry_after, the crate publishes the copy to the waiting queue with the delay as its expiration, then acknowledges the original. Both frames go out on one channel in that order, so a connection lost between them brings the original back rather than losing it. The waiting queue has no consumers. When the TTL fires, it dead-letters the copy back to the origin queue on the default exchange. The copy lives on the broker, so it survives a restart of the service. The waiting queue is <queue>.retry; Delay::dlx_ttl_named names another. The released copy is a new message to the server, and it carries x-ruststream-retry-count raised by one. So a retry cap ends a delayed loop the way it ends an immediate one. A waiting queue releases expired messages only from its head, so a short delay waits behind a long one. Mixed delays take one waiting queue per delay class, or the delayed-message plugin. The waiting queue is infrastructure. With declare_topology(true) the service declares it: durable, dead-lettering to the origin queue. On a broker that declares nothing, the operator provisions it with those arguments. The subscription checks at startup that the waiting queue exists, and the service fails to start without it.

A shipment that arrives while the warehouse is closed waits a minute in shipments.retry. The released copy carries the retry count, and the shipment goes out. Macros Manual examples/lapin_settlement_delay.rs /// A shipment that arrives while the warehouse is closed waits a minute in `shipments.retry`, on /// the broker. The copy it releases carries the retry count, and the shipment goes out. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("shipments").delay(Delay::dlx_ttl()))] async fn dispatch(shipment: &Shipment, ctx: &mut Context<'_>) -> HandlerOutcome { if ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).is_none() { tracing::info!(shipment.id, "warehouse closed, waiting"); return HandlerOutcome::retry_after(WAIT); } tracing::info!(shipment.id, "dispatched"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { // The service declares its queues, `shipments.retry` included. let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shipping", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(dispatch); }) } examples/manual/lapin_settlement_delay.rs /// A shipment that arrives while the warehouse is closed waits a minute in `shipments.retry`, on /// the broker. The copy it releases carries the retry count, and the shipment goes out. struct Dispatch; impl Handle<Shipment> for Dispatch { fn handle( &self, shipment: &Shipment, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).is_none() { tracing::info!(shipment.id, "warehouse closed, waiting"); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(WAIT))); } tracing::info!(shipment.id, "dispatched"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { // The service declares its queues, `shipments.retry` included. let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shipping", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let shipments = RabbitQueue::new("shipments").delay(Delay::dlx_ttl()); b.include(subscriber(shipments, Dispatch).build()); }) }

delivery_limit(n) sets a quorum queue's x-delivery-limit: how many times the queue returns a message before it carries it away. The argument counts returns, so the queue delivers a message n + 1 times: delivery_limit(4) delivers it five times. A quorum queue counts a delivery the handler rejected and a delivery whose consumer went away without settling it. Once the count passes the limit, the queue sends the message to its dead-letter exchange, or drops it when it has none. The server applies the limit itself: it holds while no service is running, and the service publishes nothing. A quorum queue without a limit of its own takes RabbitMQ's default of 20 returns. A returned message carries the queue's count in the x-delivery-count header. A registration states the same through the mount chain: max_attempts(n) and dead_letter(name). On a quorum queue the pair becomes an x-delivery-limit of n - 1 and a dead-letter route to the queue name, written over the descriptor's limit. The pair reaches the queue only when the service declares it, so the broker sets declare_topology(true). On a broker that declares nothing the subscription refuses to start, and so does half of the pair. out_retry(policy) does not compile on a quorum queue, because no copy leaves this process.

The provider refuses a charge every time. The queue delivers it five times and then moves it to charges.dlx, where a classic queue keeps it. Macros Manual examples/lapin_settlement_delivery_limit.rs /// The provider refuses this charge every time. The queue returns it four times, so it is /// delivered five times, and then the queue moves it to `charges.dlx`. #[subscriber(RabbitQuorumQueue::new("charges") .delivery_limit(4) .dead_letter_exchange("charges.dlx"))] async fn take_payment(charge: &Charge) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::warn!(charge.id, "provider refused the charge"); HandlerOutcome::retry() } /// The charges the queue gave up on. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("charges.parked").bind(RabbitExchange::fanout("charges.dlx"), ""))] async fn park(charge: &Charge) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::error!(charge.id, "charge parked"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(take_payment); b.include(park); }) } examples/manual/lapin_settlement_delivery_limit.rs /// The provider refuses this charge every time. The queue returns it four times, so it is /// delivered five times, and then the queue moves it to `charges.dlx`. struct TakePayment; impl Handle<Charge> for TakePayment { fn handle( &self, charge: &Charge, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::warn!(charge.id, "provider refused the charge"); ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry())) } } /// The charges the queue gave up on. struct Park; impl Handle<Charge> for Park { fn handle( &self, charge: &Charge, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::error!(charge.id, "charge parked"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let charges = RabbitQuorumQueue::new("charges") .delivery_limit(4) .dead_letter_exchange("charges.dlx"); let parked = RabbitQueue::new("charges.parked").bind(RabbitExchange::fanout("charges.dlx"), ""); b.include(subscriber(charges, TakePayment).build()); b.include(subscriber(parked, Park).build()); }) }

Delay::plugin_dme hands a delayed copy to RabbitMQ's delayed-message-exchange plugin instead of a waiting queue. The crate publishes the copy to an x-delayed-message exchange with the delay in its x-delay header, then acknowledges the original. The plugin holds each message for its own delay and then routes it to the origin queue. So a short delay never waits behind a long one, and one exchange serves every delay. The exchange is <queue>.delay; Delay::plugin_dme_named names another, which several queues may share. The released copy carries x-ruststream-retry-count raised by one, as with a waiting queue. The backend sits behind the crate's plugin-dme feature, and the plugin has to be enabled on the server. With declare_topology(true) the service declares the exchange and binds the origin queue to it. On a broker that declares nothing, the operator provisions both, and the subscription checks at startup that the exchange exists.

Each reminder waits as long as it asks for. The in-process transport releases the copy like a waiting queue; the plugin's own release order shows only against a server with the plugin. Macros Manual examples/lapin_settlement_plugin_dme.rs /// Each reminder waits as long as it asks, in the plugin's exchange `reminders.delay`. A short /// wait is released on time even while a long one is still held. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("reminders").delay(Delay::plugin_dme()))] async fn remind(reminder: &Reminder, ctx: &mut Context<'_>) -> HandlerOutcome { if ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).is_none() { return HandlerOutcome::retry_after(Duration::from_secs(reminder.after_secs)); } tracing::info!(reminder.id, "reminder sent"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { // The service declares the delayed exchange; the plugin has to be enabled on the server. let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reminders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(remind); }) } examples/manual/lapin_settlement_plugin_dme.rs /// Each reminder waits as long as it asks, in the plugin's exchange `reminders.delay`. A short /// wait is released on time even while a long one is still held. struct Remind; impl Handle<Reminder> for Remind { fn handle( &self, reminder: &Reminder, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).is_none() { let wait = Duration::from_secs(reminder.after_secs); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(wait))); } tracing::info!(reminder.id, "reminder sent"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { // The service declares the delayed exchange; the plugin has to be enabled on the server. let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reminders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let reminders = RabbitQueue::new("reminders").delay(Delay::plugin_dme()); b.include(subscriber(reminders, Remind).build()); }) }

max_attempts(n) and dead_letter(name) cap the deliveries of one message; on a classic queue the runtime keeps the count. max_attempts(n) is how many deliveries one message gets, the first included. dead_letter(name) is where it goes once they run out. A classic queue counts nothing, so under a cap every retry, an immediate one too, travels as a copy. The runtime settles the delivery and publishes a copy of the message back to the queue. The copy carries RETRY_COUNT_HEADER (x-ruststream-retry-count) raised by one, and the handler reads it like any other header. The copy goes back under the queue's own name: on the default exchange a routing key addresses the queue of that name. The delivery that reaches the cap is published under name instead, so name is the queue the message lands in, with its count. A bare queue name, #[subscriber("payments")], takes the same cap. The copies leave through the broker's default publish policy. out_retry(policy) names another one, and the position takes a slot's steps: .codec(..), .transform(..), .to(name). The example names the confirms policy, whose publish resolves once the broker has confirmed the copy. A retry policy aimed at a topic or direct exchange reaches the queue only through a binding under the queue's name. On a quorum queue the same two steps become the queue's own delivery limit.

A declined card is retried at once. The third delivery is the last: the payment goes to payments.dead, where a second subscription reads the count. Macros Manual examples/lapin_settlement_retries.rs /// A card the gateway declines is asked for again, at once. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("payments"))] async fn charge(payment: &Payment) -> HandlerOutcome { if payment.card.starts_with("0000") { tracing::warn!(payment.id, "card declined, retrying"); return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// The payments that ran out of deliveries, with the count the runtime kept. #[subscriber("payments.dead")] async fn bury(payment: &Payment, ctx: &mut Context<'_>) -> HandlerOutcome { let deliveries = ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).unwrap_or("1"); tracing::error!(payment.id, deliveries, "payment dead-lettered"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { // Three deliveries, the first included, then the payment goes to `payments.dead`. The // copies leave through the confirms policy, which waits for the broker to confirm each. b.include(charge) .max_attempts(nonzero!(3u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead") .out_retry(TransactionalPublish::default()); b.include(bury); }) } examples/manual/lapin_settlement_retries.rs /// A card the gateway declines is asked for again, at once. struct Charge; impl Handle<Payment> for Charge { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if payment.card.starts_with("0000") { tracing::warn!(payment.id, "card declined, retrying"); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry())); } ready(Ok(())) } } /// The payments that ran out of deliveries, with the count the runtime kept. struct Bury; impl Handle<Payment> for Bury { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { let deliveries = ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).unwrap_or("1"); tracing::error!(payment.id, deliveries, "payment dead-lettered"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { // Three deliveries, the first included, then the payment goes to `payments.dead`. The // copies leave through the confirms policy, which waits for the broker to confirm each. b.include(subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("payments"), Charge).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(3u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead") .out_retry(TransactionalPublish::default()); b.include(subscriber("payments.dead", Bury).build()); }) }

retry_after(delay) asks for a redelivery no sooner than delay, for a message that is not ready yet. AMQP has no per-message delay, so on a queue without a delay the runtime waits. It settles the delivery, holds a copy in the service and publishes it back to the queue when the delay is up. The copy goes out under the queue's name on the default exchange, which addresses the queue of that name. It carries RETRY_COUNT_HEADER raised by one. The copy lives in the service's memory, so it is at-most-once over the delay: a process that stops before the timer fires loses it. A retry cap counts these copies like immediate ones.

The first delivery finds the payment unsettled and asks for the refund again in 30 seconds. The copy comes back with the retry count, and the refund goes through. Macros Manual examples/lapin_settlement_retry_after.rs /// The first delivery finds the payment unsettled and asks for the refund again in 30 seconds. /// The copy that comes back carries the retry count, and the refund goes through. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("refunds"))] async fn issue_refund(refund: &Refund, ctx: &mut Context<'_>) -> HandlerOutcome { if ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).is_none() { tracing::info!(refund.id, "payment not settled yet"); return HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK); } tracing::info!(refund.id, "refunded"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("refunds", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(issue_refund); }, ) } examples/manual/lapin_settlement_retry_after.rs /// The first delivery finds the payment unsettled and asks for the refund again in 30 seconds. /// The copy that comes back carries the retry count, and the refund goes through. struct IssueRefund; impl Handle<Refund> for IssueRefund { fn handle( &self, refund: &Refund, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).is_none() { tracing::info!(refund.id, "payment not settled yet"); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK))); } tracing::info!(refund.id, "refunded"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("refunds", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("refunds"), IssueRefund).build()); }, ) }

A queue name in #[subscriber] consumes that existing queue as a classic queue; a descriptor carries every other setting. One subscription consumes one queue. #[subscriber("orders")] consumes the queue orders with the defaults of RabbitQueue: a durable classic queue, the broker's prefetch and no bindings. The queue has to exist on the server, unless the broker declares the topology. A message reaches it through the default exchange, which routes on the queue's name, or through an exchange the queue is bound to. RabbitMQ has two queue types, and the type is fixed when the queue is created. The type decides what a retry does, so each type has a descriptor of its own: Descriptor Queue A retry is RabbitQueue classic, on one node counted by the runtime, on the copies it publishes back RabbitQuorumQueue quorum, replicated counted by the server, which ends a message that spent its deliveries A descriptor goes where the name goes, as the attribute's first argument, and every one of its steps returns the descriptor. The manual form passes the name or the descriptor to subscriber(source, body). Several instances of a service share one queue, and each message goes to one of them. The handler's outcome is a protocol frame: an ack removes the message, and a retry or a drop rejects it, as the Settlement pages show. With automatic recovery enabled, a subscription waits while Lapin restores its channel and consumer, then resumes through the same handle. Unsettled deliveries may be redelivered after an outage, so handlers must tolerate duplicates. When retries run out, the stream yields a consume error and ends. Recovery is disabled by default.

An order with items is acknowledged; an empty order is dropped. Macros Manual examples/lapin_subscriptions_queue.rs use ruststream_lapin::prelude::*; #[subscriber("orders")] async fn place(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { if order.items == 0 { tracing::warn!(order.id, "empty order dropped"); return HandlerOutcome::drop(); } tracing::info!(order.id, order.items, "order placed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(place); }, ) } examples/manual/lapin_subscriptions_queue.rs use ruststream_lapin::prelude::*; struct Place; impl Handle<Order> for Place { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if order.items == 0 { tracing::warn!(order.id, "empty order dropped"); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::drop())); } tracing::info!(order.id, order.items, "order placed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(subscriber("orders", Place).build()); }, ) }

argument and arguments pass any x- declaration argument the descriptor does not model, such as a TTL or a length limit, verbatim. A queue declaration carries a table of arguments, and RabbitMQ reads queue features from it: x-message-ttl, x-max-length, x-overflow, x-single-active-consumer and more. argument(name, value) adds one entry, and arguments(table) replaces the whole table. The value is an AMQPValue and the table a FieldTable, both re-exported from lapin. A name is at most 255 bytes, the protocol's limit for a field name. The settings the descriptor models, such as the dead-letter exchange and the queue type, travel in the same table, so they are written with their own steps. The arguments reach the server in the queue's declaration, so they take effect where the broker declares the topology. A queue keeps the arguments it was first declared with. A declaration with other arguments is refused with PRECONDITION_FAILED, and startup fails with AmqpError::Declare; the in-process transport refuses it the same way. What an argument does to the messages, such as a TTL that expires them, is the server's work and shows only against a server.

Notifications expire after a minute, and the queue holds at most ten thousand of them. The macro form adds the arguments one by one; the manual form builds the table. Macros Manual examples/lapin_subscriptions_arguments.rs /// A notification older than a minute is no longer worth sending, and the queue keeps at most /// ten thousand of them. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("notifications") .argument("x-message-ttl", AMQPValue::LongLongInt(60_000)) .argument("x-max-length", AMQPValue::LongLongInt(10_000)))] async fn notify(notification: &Notification) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(notification.user, "notification sent"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/lapin_subscriptions_arguments.rs struct Notify; impl Handle<Notification> for Notify { fn handle( &self, notification: &Notification, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(notification.user, "notification sent"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// A notification older than a minute is no longer worth sending, and the queue keeps at most /// ten thousand of them. fn notifications() -> RabbitQueue { let mut arguments = FieldTable::default(); arguments.insert("x-message-ttl".into(), AMQPValue::LongLongInt(60_000)); arguments.insert("x-max-length".into(), AMQPValue::LongLongInt(10_000)); RabbitQueue::new("notifications").arguments(arguments) }

A slice handler gets a batch assembled on the client, up to the mount site's size or until batch_wait (50 ms) passes since the first delivery. A handler over &[T] is a batch handler, and batch(n) at the mount site is its largest batch. AMQP pushes one delivery at a time, so the subscription collects deliveries into a batch on the client. A batch closes when it holds n deliveries, or when batch_wait has passed since its first delivery, 50 ms by default. A raised wait gives fuller batches on a sparse queue; a lowered one hands a short batch over sooner. The server sends no more than the prefetch window, so a window below n keeps every batch below n. One outcome settles every delivery of the batch. In the manual form the body is an impl Handle<[T]>: Ok(()) acknowledges the batch, and Err(outcomes) settles delivery i with outcome i. workers(n) keeps up to n batches in flight at once.

Payments settle up to 32 at a time, and a batch that does not fill closes 200 ms after its first payment. Macros Manual examples/lapin_subscriptions_batches.rs use ruststream_lapin::prelude::*; /// Settles up to 32 payments in one call; a batch that does not fill closes 200 ms after its /// first payment arrived. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("payments") .prefetch(nonzero!(64)) .batch_wait(Duration::from_millis(200)))] async fn settle(payments: &[Payment]) -> HandlerOutcome { let cents: u64 = payments.iter().map(|payment| payment.cents).sum(); tracing::info!(count = payments.len(), cents, "payments settled"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(settle.batch(nonzero!(32))); }, ) } examples/manual/lapin_subscriptions_batches.rs use ruststream_lapin::prelude::*; /// Settles a batch of payments; `Ok` acknowledges the whole batch. struct Settle; impl Handle<[Payment]> for Settle { fn handle( &self, payments: &[Payment], _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Vec<HandlerOutcome>>> { let cents: u64 = payments.iter().map(|payment| payment.cents).sum(); tracing::info!(count = payments.len(), cents, "payments settled"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { // Up to 32 payments per call; a batch that does not fill closes 200 ms after its // first payment arrived. let payments = RabbitQueue::new("payments") .prefetch(nonzero!(64)) .batch_wait(Duration::from_millis(200)); b.include(subscriber(payments, Settle).batch(nonzero!(32)).build()); }, ) }

workers(n, by_key) keeps deliveries that share the amqp-partition-key header on one lane, in order, while other keys run in parallel. workers(n, by_key) runs n sequential lanes over one queue. The lane of a delivery is picked by a hash of its partition key, so deliveries with one key run one after another, in queue order. Deliveries with different keys run at once on different lanes. A delivery without a key goes to the next lane in rotation. On RabbitMQ the key is the header PARTITION_KEY_HEADER, amqp-partition-key. AMQP gives the header no meaning: it is a convention between the publisher, which sets it, and this crate, which reads it back. A service that publishes to a keyed queue sets the header on each message, such as the tenant or the account the message belongs to. The lanes order work inside one service instance. Spreading a stream over several queues by key is the consistent-hash exchange, which the server runs. The manual form writes the lanes as .workers_by_key(n) on the mount chain.

Orders of one tenant run in order on one lane, and different tenants run side by side. Macros Manual examples/lapin_subscriptions_lanes.rs use ruststream_lapin::prelude::*; /// Eight lanes: one tenant's orders never run at the same time, and different tenants run side /// by side. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("orders"), workers(8, by_key))] async fn place(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, order.tenant, "order placed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(place); }, ) } examples/manual/lapin_subscriptions_lanes.rs use ruststream_lapin::prelude::*; struct Place; impl Handle<Order> for Place { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, order.tenant, "order placed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { // Eight lanes: one tenant's orders never run at the same time, and different // tenants run side by side. let orders = RabbitQueue::new("orders"); b.include( subscriber(orders, Place) .workers_by_key(nonzero!(8)) .build(), ); }, ) }

prefetch caps unacknowledged deliveries per subscription on the broker or one descriptor; unset, the server applies no limit. The server pushes deliveries to a consumer without waiting to be asked. The prefetch window (basic.qos) is how many deliveries it may have out to one subscription before the service settles some of them. So the window is the back-pressure between a queue and a service: a slow handler holds the rest of the queue on the server, where other instances can take it. LapinBroker::prefetch sets the window for every subscription of the broker. RabbitQueue::prefetch and RabbitQuorumQueue::prefetch set it for one subscription and take precedence. The count is a NonZeroU16, because AMQP reads a window of 0 as no limit. A subscription with neither setting has no window, and the server pushes it the whole queue. A batch handler needs a window of at least its batch size, or its batches stay short. The window is the server's: the in-process transport has none and hands a subscription everything its queue holds. A test of the window runs against a server with TestApp::start_live.

Every subscription holds up to 64 deliveries, and the slow report queue holds one. Macros Manual examples/lapin_subscriptions_prefetch.rs use ruststream_lapin::prelude::*; #[subscriber("orders")] async fn place(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// A report takes minutes to render, so this instance holds one at a time and leaves the rest /// to the other instances. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("reports").prefetch(nonzero!(1)))] async fn render(report: &Report) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(report.id, "report rendered"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { // Every subscription holds up to 64 unacknowledged deliveries, unless its descriptor says // otherwise. let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").prefetch(nonzero!(64)); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(place); b.include(render); }) } examples/manual/lapin_subscriptions_prefetch.rs use ruststream_lapin::prelude::*; struct Place; impl Handle<Order> for Place { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// A report takes minutes to render, so this instance holds one at a time and leaves the rest /// to the other instances. struct Render; impl Handle<Report> for Render { fn handle( &self, report: &Report, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(report.id, "report rendered"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { // Every subscription holds up to 64 unacknowledged deliveries, unless its descriptor says // otherwise. let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").prefetch(nonzero!(64)); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(subscriber("orders", Place).build()); let reports = RabbitQueue::new("reports").prefetch(nonzero!(1)); b.include(subscriber(reports, Render).build()); }) }

RabbitQueue consumes a classic queue: its durability, exclusivity, auto-delete, bindings and the settings shared with quorum queues. RabbitQueue::new names the queue. Three settings belong to the classic queue alone: Setting Default What it does durable true the queue survives a broker restart exclusive false the queue belongs to the connection that declared it and goes with it auto_delete false the server deletes the queue once its last consumer leaves RabbitMQ 4 refuses a transient queue that other connections may share, so durable(false) comes with exclusive(true). An exclusive queue suits a per-instance feed, such as a cache that every instance refreshes from a fanout exchange. The other settings are shared with RabbitQuorumQueue: bind and bind_with join the queue to exchanges, dead_letter_exchange and dead_letter_routing_key give it a route for rejected messages, prefetch and batch_wait shape its consumption, delay parks delayed retries on the server, and argument passes anything else the queue declaration takes. Bindings, the dead-letter route and the arguments reach the server when the broker declares the topology. A classic queue keeps no count of a message's deliveries. A retry puts the message back on the queue, and its next delivery carries the redelivered flag, which a handler reads through the Redelivered key.

The order queue is bound to a topic exchange and dead-letters to orders.failed; an order that fails once is placed on its redelivery. The price queue belongs to this instance alone. Macros Manual examples/lapin_subscriptions_rabbit_queue.rs /// A durable queue fed by the topic exchange `events`; a dropped order leaves through /// `orders.failed`. A delivery the server already handed out once is placed on its second try. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("orders") .bind(RabbitExchange::topic("events"), "order.*") .dead_letter_exchange("orders.failed"))] async fn place(order: &Order, Ctx(redelivered): Ctx<Redelivered>) -> HandlerOutcome { if !redelivered && order.flaky { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } tracing::info!(order.id, redelivered, "order placed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// A queue of this instance alone: it lives as long as the connection that declared it. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("prices.instance-a") .durable(false) .exclusive(true) .auto_delete(true) .bind(RabbitExchange::fanout("prices"), ""))] async fn refresh(price: &Price) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(price.sku, price.cents, "price cached"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/lapin_subscriptions_rabbit_queue.rs /// A delivery the server already handed out once is placed on its second try. struct Place; impl Handle<Order, (), (), AmqpContext> for Place { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, AmqpContext>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { let redelivered = ctx.context(Redelivered); if !redelivered && order.flaky { return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry())); } tracing::info!(order.id, redelivered, "order placed"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// A durable queue fed by the topic exchange `events`; a dropped order leaves through /// `orders.failed`. fn orders() -> RabbitQueue { RabbitQueue::new("orders") .bind(RabbitExchange::topic("events"), "order.*") .dead_letter_exchange("orders.failed") } struct Refresh; impl Handle<Price> for Refresh { fn handle( &self, price: &Price, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(price.sku, price.cents, "price cached"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// A queue of this instance alone: it lives as long as the connection that declared it. fn prices() -> RabbitQueue { RabbitQueue::new("prices.instance-a") .durable(false) .exclusive(true) .auto_delete(true) .bind(RabbitExchange::fanout("prices"), "") }

RabbitQuorumQueue consumes a replicated quorum queue, which is always durable and counts the deliveries each message spends. A quorum queue keeps its messages on several nodes through Raft, so it survives the loss of a node. It is durable, shared and permanent by definition. So the descriptor has no durable, exclusive or auto_delete step, and a quorum queue that contradicts its type does not compile. Every shared setting of RabbitQueue is on it too. The server counts each delivery of a message, and a retry spends one. A quorum delivery reports its count, where a classic delivery reports only the redelivered flag. Past the queue's delivery limit the server takes the message off the queue: it dead-letters the message when the queue has a dead-letter exchange, and drops it otherwise. RabbitMQ 4 gives a quorum queue a limit of 20 when it names none, so a message that keeps failing gets 21 deliveries. delivery_limit sets another limit; max_attempts with dead_letter at the mount site sets it from the registration. The queue type is part of the declaration, so a quorum queue is created by an operator or by a broker that declares the topology. A quorum queue refuses some classic arguments: a declaration with x-max-priority fails with AmqpError::Declare.

A reservation waits for stock; one that never fits ends after the queue's default delivery limit. Macros Manual examples/lapin_subscriptions_quorum.rs use ruststream_lapin::prelude::*; /// A reservation waits for stock; the queue gives up on one after its delivery limit. #[subscriber(RabbitQuorumQueue::new("reservations"))] async fn reserve(reservation: &Reservation) -> HandlerOutcome { if !reservation.in_stock { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } tracing::info!(reservation.id, "reserved"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reservations", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(reserve); }) } examples/manual/lapin_subscriptions_quorum.rs use ruststream_lapin::prelude::*; /// A reservation waits for stock; the queue gives up on one after its delivery limit. struct Reserve; impl Handle<Reservation> for Reserve { fn handle( &self, reservation: &Reservation, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if !reservation.in_stock { return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry())); } tracing::info!(reservation.id, "reserved"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reservations", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let reservations = RabbitQuorumQueue::new("reservations"); b.include(subscriber(reservations, Reserve).build()); }) }

TestApp::start runs the production app on LapinBroker in process, with exchanges, bindings, requeues, quorum counts and reply-to. A test hands the harness the app main runs, unchanged, and addresses the broker by its production type, tb.broker::<LapinBroker>(). The testing feature in [dev-dependencies] adds the in-process mode, and turns on the core's harness with it. The in-process transport has no settings of its own. It reads the broker's: declare_topology decides whether a subscription declares its queue, as on the server. A publish is framed by the same conversion a publish to the server goes through. The transport keeps RabbitMQ's semantics. The default exchange and the direct, topic, fanout and headers exchanges route through the bindings the descriptors declare. Consumers of one queue compete for its messages, and a requeue puts a message back in its queue. A queue keeps what reaches it from its first subscription on, until an auto-delete queue loses its last consumer. A consumer that closes returns what it took and left unsettled. A quorum queue counts deliveries and dead-letters a spent one through its route. A waiting queue releases a delayed copy, and direct reply-to gives every request an address of its own. The transport refuses what the server refuses, with the same error. That covers a name over 255 bytes, a header the frame cannot carry, and a body over the server's default max_message_size of 16 MiB. It covers the declarations the server refuses: a transient queue that is not exclusive, a binding on the default exchange, a queue declared again with other settings, a quorum queue with a priority. A delivery settled after its connection closed reports the closed channel. A publish through the harness returns once every handler it woke has settled, a reply or a slot publish included. The assertions that follow read finished state. What only a server has is for a live test: the prefetch window, publisher confirms, the atomicity of a server transaction, a plugin exchange's routing, a queue two connections share, and a topology the service finds without declaring it.

The dependency line: [dev-dependencies] ruststream-lapin = { version = "0.7", features = ["testing"] } The first test publishes a payment and reads how the handler settled it. TestApp::start_live runs the same test body against a running RabbitMQ, one subscription per queue, for what only a server has. It connects the broker through its ordinary connect, so every subscription consumes from the server. The body is the one an in-process test runs; only the start call differs. A publish, settle and advance wait on the real clock until every subscription has handled what was published to it. The wait lasts ten seconds at most, and start_live_within sets another bound. The live mode is for what the in-process transport leaves to the server: the prefetch window, publisher confirms, the atomicity of a server transaction, a plugin exchange's routing, and a topology the service finds without declaring it. A live test keeps one subscription per queue. The server picks which consumer of a queue takes a message, so a test with two subscriptions of one queue stops at the first publish and names the queue. A server keeps what earlier runs left in it. In the example the service declares its queue with declare_topology, and the queue is exclusive: it lives as long as the test's connection. live::url is the repository's test helper: it returns the server's address from AMQP_TEST_URL, and the test returns early without one, so cargo test passes on a machine with no server. A job that stood a server up sets RUSTSTREAM_REQUIRE_LIVE=1, and a missing address then fails the test instead of skipping it. The repository's stand is docker-compose.test.yml, which just brokers-up starts.

The two tests share one body: one in process, one against the server at AMQP_TEST_URL. A handler bounded Out<impl TransactionalPublisher> opens a transaction scope with begin, publishes through it, and ends it with commit or abort. The scope's publishes become visible together at commit, and abort discards them. The handler names the capability, TransactionalPublisher, and the mount site names the policy that provides it. ConfirmsPublish, TransactionalPublish in the prelude, buffers in the client and commits by awaiting a broker confirm for every message. ServerTxPublish runs an AMQP channel transaction on the server. LapinPublish pairs into a publisher with no transaction surface, so a transactional handler mounted with it does not compile. A publisher runs one such transaction at a time. A second begin while one is open, or a commit or abort with none open, fails with AmqpError::Transaction and leaves the open transaction as it was. A publisher is a shared handle: every clone uses one channel and one transaction state. Several independent groups of messages in one handler take the owned kind, ConfirmsTransaction.

An order ships one message per item, in one transaction. An item without a name aborts the transaction, and the shipments already published are discarded. Macros Manual examples/lapin_transactions_scope.rs /// One shipment per item, in one transaction. An item without a name aborts it, and the shipments /// already published are discarded with it. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("orders"))] async fn ship(order: &Order, Out(shipments): Out<impl TransactionalPublisher>) -> HandlerOutcome { let Ok(scope) = shipments.begin().await else { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); }; for item in &order.items { if item.is_empty() { tracing::warn!(order.id, "an item without a name, nothing shipped"); return match scope.abort().await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::drop(), Err(_) => HandlerOutcome::retry(), }; } let shipment = Shipment { order_id: order.id, item: item.clone(), }; if scope.message(&shipment).publish().await.is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } } if scope.commit().await.is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/lapin_transactions_scope.rs /// One shipment per item, in one transaction. An item without a name aborts it, and the shipments /// already published are discarded with it. struct Ship; impl<Egress> Handle<Order, (), Outs<(Egress,)>> for Ship where Egress: OutEntry<DefaultSlot, Wire: TransactionalPublisher>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(Egress,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let scope = outs .get(DefaultSlot) .begin() .await .map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry())?; for item in &order.items { if item.is_empty() { tracing::warn!(order.id, "an item without a name, nothing shipped"); scope.abort().await.map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry())?; return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); } let shipment = Shipment { order_id: order.id, item: item.clone(), }; if scope.message(&shipment).publish().await.is_err() { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } } scope.commit().await.map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()) } } Macros Manual examples/lapin_transactions_scope.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { // The confirms policy; `LapinPublish::default().server_tx()` is the other one. b.include(ship) .out(DefaultSlot, TransactionalPublish::default()) .build(); }, ) } examples/manual/lapin_transactions_scope.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { // The confirms policy; `LapinPublish::default().server_tx()` is the other one. b.include(subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("orders"), Ship).build()) .out(DefaultSlot, TransactionalPublish::default()) .build(); }, ) }

ConfirmsPublish, TransactionalPublish in the prelude, is the publish policy whose every publish resolves once the broker has confirmed the message. LapinPublish::confirms reaches it with the same settings: exchange and property defaults. It pairs into a ConfirmsPublisher with a confirm channel of its own. A message the broker refuses fails the publish, and the handler decides what follows. RabbitMQ confirms a message once it has routed it, and a message that matches no queue is confirmed and dropped. So a confirm says the broker took the message, not that a queue holds it. Inside a transaction the publisher buffers in the client. commit publishes the buffer in order and resolves once every message is confirmed, and abort discards the buffer without touching the broker. A failed commit loses the buffer, and the delivery's redelivery is the way to recover. The policy offers the borrowed kind of the transaction scope and the owned kind of ConfirmsTransaction.

A payment is acknowledged once the broker has confirmed its receipt. A receipt the broker refused brings the payment back. Macros Manual examples/lapin_transactions_confirms.rs /// The payment is acknowledged once the broker has confirmed its receipt. A receipt the broker /// refused brings the payment back. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("payments"))] async fn settle(payment: &Payment, Out(receipts): Out<impl Publisher>) -> HandlerOutcome { let receipt = Receipt { payment_id: payment.id, }; if let Err(err) = receipts.message(&receipt).publish().await { tracing::warn!(payment.id, %err, "receipt not confirmed"); return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } tracing::info!(payment.id, payment.cents, "payment settled"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(settle) .out(DefaultSlot, TransactionalPublish::default()) .build(); }) } examples/manual/lapin_transactions_confirms.rs /// The payment is acknowledged once the broker has confirmed its receipt. A receipt the broker /// refused brings the payment back. struct Settle; impl<Egress> Handle<Payment, (), Outs<(Egress,)>> for Settle where Egress: OutEntry<DefaultSlot, Wire: Publisher>, { async fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, outs: &Outs<(Egress,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let receipt = Receipt { payment_id: payment.id, }; let receipts = outs.get(DefaultSlot); if let Err(err) = receipts.message(&receipt).publish().await { tracing::warn!(payment.id, %err, "receipt not confirmed"); return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } tracing::info!(payment.id, payment.cents, "payment settled"); Ok(()) } } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("payments"), Settle).build()) .out(DefaultSlot, TransactionalPublish::default()) .build(); }) }

ConfirmsTransaction is an owned confirm transaction: a value that holds its own publish buffer. A handler bounded Out<impl OwnedTransactions, Slot> opens one with transaction() on its slot, and every call opens another. Any number can be open on one publisher, and settling one never touches another. The publisher keeps publishing directly while they are open. commit publishes the buffer in order and awaits every confirm, and abort discards it without touching the broker. Both consume the value, so a double commit or a publish after settling does not compile. A failed commit loses the buffer, and the delivery's redelivery is the way to recover. Only ConfirmsPublish offers the owned kind.

The shipment and the audit record of an order go out in two transactions. An order out of stock aborts the shipment and still commits its audit record. Macros Manual examples/lapin_transactions_owned.rs #[derive(OutSlot)] #[publishes(Shipment, AuditRecord)] struct Records; /// The shipment and the audit record go out in two transactions. The shipment waits in its own /// buffer while the stock is checked: an order out of stock aborts it and still commits its audit /// record. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("orders"))] async fn record( order: &Order, Out(records): Out<impl OwnedTransactions, Records>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { let (Ok(mut shipment), Ok(mut audit)) = (records.transaction().await, records.transaction().await) else { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); }; let shipped = Shipment { order_id: order.id }; if shipment.message(&shipped).publish().await.is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } let settled = if order.in_stock { shipment.commit().await } else { shipment.abort().await }; if settled.is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } let entry = AuditRecord { order_id: order.id, shipped: order.in_stock, }; if audit.message(&entry).publish().await.is_err() || audit.commit().await.is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(record) .out(Records, TransactionalPublish::default()) .build(); }, ) } examples/manual/lapin_transactions_owned.rs #[derive(OutSlot)] #[publishes(Shipment, AuditRecord)] struct Records; /// The shipment and the audit record go out in two transactions. The shipment waits in its own /// buffer while the stock is checked: an order out of stock aborts it and still commits its audit /// record. struct Record; impl<Egress> Handle<Order, (), Outs<(Egress,)>> for Record where Egress: OutEntry<Records, Wire: OwnedTransactions>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(Egress,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let records = outs.get(Records); let (Ok(mut shipment), Ok(mut audit)) = (records.transaction().await, records.transaction().await) else { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); }; let shipped = Shipment { order_id: order.id }; if shipment.message(&shipped).publish().await.is_err() { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } let settled = if order.in_stock { shipment.commit().await } else { shipment.abort().await }; if settled.is_err() { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } let entry = AuditRecord { order_id: order.id, shipped: order.in_stock, }; if audit.message(&entry).publish().await.is_err() || audit.commit().await.is_err() { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } Ok(()) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("orders"), Record).build()) .out(Records, TransactionalPublish::default()) .build(); }, ) }

ServerTxPublish is the publish policy backed by AMQP channel transactions: tx.select, tx.commit and tx.rollback. LapinPublish::server_tx reaches it with the same settings. It pairs into a ServerTxPublisher on a channel of its own. Between begin and commit the messages wait on the broker inside the channel transaction, and they become visible together at commit. abort rolls them back on the server. Each commit is a synchronous round trip, which makes the policy slower than ConfirmsPublish. Outside a transaction a publish behaves like a fire-and-forget one. The transaction is the channel's state, so the policy offers only the borrowed kind of the transaction scope. Server transactions require auto_recover(false), which is the default. Lapin cannot restore a transaction's state after a disconnect, so pairing this policy with auto_recover(true) fails with AmqpError::InvalidOptions before it is used. Direct publish, begin, commit and abort calls also reject that combination. Use publisher confirms when enabling connection recovery.

The debit and the credit of a transfer are published in one server transaction. A frozen account rolls it back, and the debit already sent is discarded on the broker. Macros Manual examples/lapin_transactions_server_tx.rs /// The debit and the credit of a transfer are published in one server transaction. A frozen /// account rolls it back, and the debit already sent is discarded on the broker. #[subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("transfers"))] async fn book( transfer: &Transfer, Out(ledger): Out<impl TransactionalPublisher>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { let Ok(scope) = ledger.begin().await else { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); }; let legs = [ (transfer.from, -transfer.cents), (transfer.to, transfer.cents), ]; for (account, cents) in legs { if account == FROZEN { tracing::warn!(account, "frozen account, transfer rolled back"); return match scope.abort().await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::drop(), Err(_) => HandlerOutcome::retry(), }; } if scope .message(&Entry { account, cents }) .publish() .await .is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } } if scope.commit().await.is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ledger", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(book) .out(DefaultSlot, ServerTxPublish::default()) .build(); }, ) } examples/manual/lapin_transactions_server_tx.rs /// The debit and the credit of a transfer are published in one server transaction. A frozen /// account rolls it back, and the debit already sent is discarded on the broker. struct Book; impl<Egress> Handle<Transfer, (), Outs<(Egress,)>> for Book where Egress: OutEntry<DefaultSlot, Wire: TransactionalPublisher>, { async fn handle( &self, transfer: &Transfer, outs: &Outs<(Egress,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let scope = outs .get(DefaultSlot) .begin() .await .map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry())?; let legs = [ (transfer.from, -transfer.cents), (transfer.to, transfer.cents), ]; for (account, cents) in legs { if account == FROZEN { tracing::warn!(account, "frozen account, transfer rolled back"); scope.abort().await.map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry())?; return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); } if scope .message(&Entry { account, cents }) .publish() .await .is_err() { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } } scope.commit().await.map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ledger", "0.1.0")).with_broker( LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(subscriber(RabbitQueue::new("transfers"), Book).build()) .out(DefaultSlot, ServerTxPublish::default()) .build(); }, ) }

amqps:// URI 通过 TLS 连接，端口通常是 5671。 TLS 由 ruststream-lapin 的三个 feature 之一提供，每个都对应 lapin 自己的 feature： Feature TLS 库 tls-native-tls 平台自带的库：Linux 上是 OpenSSL，macOS 上是 Secure Transport，Windows 上是 SChannel tls-rustls rustls tls-rustls-ring 使用 ring 加密后端的 rustls 服务器证书按所选库的受信任根证书进行校验。 RabbitMQ 的 TLS 指南讲解了服务器端的配置。 TLS 组件给出了依赖声明的写法。 服务的 AsyncAPI 文档报告主机和 AMQP 版本，从不报告 URI 中的凭据或虚拟主机：这份文档会被公开和分享。
生产服务通常关闭 declare_topology 运行，使用由运维创建和修改的队列。 这时不存在的队列会让启动失败，而不是丢失消息（拓扑）。 在这种部署方式下，仲裁队列的尝试次数上限和延迟重试的等待队列同样由服务器一侧负责（确认、重试与死信）。

一个连接承载整个服务。 每个订阅打开自己的信道，所以一个队列上的错误不会让其他队列停下来。 发后即忘的发布共用一个信道。 发布者确认模式的发布者、信道事务的发布者和请求方各自在首次使用时打开自己的信道，因为发布者确认、事务和 direct reply-to 都是信道的状态。 遇到信道级错误时，例如发布到不存在的交换机，RabbitMQ 关闭这个信道。 连接保持不变，发布者在下一次调用时打开新的信道。

连接恢复默认关闭。启用 LapinBroker::auto_recover(true) 后，Lapin 使用指数退避重新连接，首次连接也会重试。 默认上限为 16 次重试；.recovery_retries(n) 可以调整上限，零表示不重试。 Lapin 通过现有句柄恢复信道、已声明的交换机、队列、绑定、预取、发布者确认和消费者。它不会重启应用，也不会重新运行启动钩子。 在 URI 中配置心跳，例如 amqp://localhost:5672?heartbeat=30，以检测静默断连。 ConnectedLapinBroker::is_connected() 可供就绪检查使用：断连期间或停机后返回 false。 返回 true 并不表示信道和拓扑已恢复完毕，也不表示工作任务正常；这项检查与运行时的服务健康状态不同。 失败的发布不会自动重发，已发出的 RPC 请求的截止时间继续计算。 ServerTxPublish 要求 auto_recover(false)，因为事务状态在重连后会丢失。 启动时耗尽重试次数会导致连接失败；启动后耗尽次数则使消费者流返回终止的消费错误并结束。 仍然存在的队列中的未确认投递会在断连后返回 RabbitMQ，并可能带着 Redelivered 标记再次投递。 重新投递要求处理器容忍重复。服务器在正常信道上取消消费者（例如删除其队列）时，订阅结束。

SIGTERM 或 Ctrl+C 停止服务。 运行时停止各个订阅，并以完整的握手关闭连接。 RabbitMQ 把服务取走而未结算的每次投递交还给它的队列，由另一个实例取走。 比连接活得更久的发布者或请求方，例如后台任务持有的那个，会返回 AmqpError::Closed，而不是向已关闭的连接发送。 如果在重连期间开始停机，等待中的消费者会被唤醒，broker 停机无需等待 RabbitMQ 恢复。现有句柄立即视为已关闭；之后恢复的连接会在后台关闭，重试次数耗尽时清理也会结束。
示例文件中的测试分别用带凭据的 amqps:// URI 和格式错误的 URI 启动服务。 在进程内，URI 的解析方式与建立连接时相同，所以服务无法用来连接的 URI 也无法启动测试。 TLS 和连接丢失需要服务器，所以要用真实服务器上的测试来检查。

本指南选择服务要在多大程度上确信 RabbitMQ 已经收下它的消息，并设置单条消息的属性。 保证是挂载点上发布策略的属性，而不是每次调用时的标志： 策略 prelude 中的名字 发布何时完成 LapinPublish Publish 帧写入连接时 ConfirmsPublish TransactionalPublish RabbitMQ 确认消息时 ServerTxPublish ServerTxPublish 信道事务提交时 示例是一个订单服务。 它把一个订单拆成每个包裹一次发货，要么全部发出，要么一个也不发，并为每次发货预约快递员，加急的排在其他发货前面。

scope.message(&shipment).publish().await?; } // Resolves once RabbitMQ confirmed every shipment of the order. scope.commit().await?; Ok(()) } #[subscriber("orders")] async fn pack_order( order: &Order, Out(shipments): Out<impl TransactionalPublisher>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { match ship_all(shipments, order).await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(err) => { tracing::warn!(order.id, %err, "order not shipped"); scope.message(&shipment).publish().await?; } // Resolves once RabbitMQ confirmed every shipment of the order. scope.commit().await?; Ok(()) } struct PackOrder; impl<Shipments> Handle<Order, (), Outs<(Shipments,)>> for PackOrder where Shipments: OutEntry<DefaultSlot, Wire: TransactionalPublisher>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(Shipments,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { ship_all(outs.get(DefaultSlot), order).await.map_err(|err| { tracing::warn!(order.id, %err, "order not shipped"); ServerTxPublish 通过 Publish::default().server_tx() 获得，它改用 AMQP 信道事务。 一个事务中的消息在 commit 时一起变得可见，commit 是一次与服务器的同步往返。 发布者确认更快，能覆盖大多数情况。 当消费者绝不能看到一组消息的一半时，例如一笔转账的两边，就用信道事务。 约束为 Out<impl TransactionalPublisher> 的处理器无需改动就能挂载在任一策略上。 用 owned_transaction 打开的 ConfirmsTransaction 拥有自己的缓冲区，而不是借用发布者：可以同时打开多个，各自独立提交。 信道事务只提供借用式的作用域，因为事务就是信道本身的状态。

let sent = if shipment.expedited { pickups .message(&pickup) .priority(9) .expiration(Duration::from_hours(1)) .publish() .await } else { pickups.message(&pickup).publish().await }; if sent.is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); 本指南通过 RabbitMQ 交换机路由消息：按路由键、发给每个绑定的队列，以及按消息头。 发布者从不直接写入队列。 它带着路由键发布到交换机，交换机把消息复制到每个绑定相匹配的队列。 在 RustStream 中，队列的绑定写在它的描述符上，消息发往哪个交换机则由发布策略决定。 路由键就是消息的名字：消息类型上的 #[outgoing(name = "..")]，或者发布时给出的名字。 示例是一家网店：它在 topic 交换机上发布订单，在 fanout 交换机上发布价格变动，在 headers 交换机上发布发货信息。 Broker 声明交换机、队列和绑定，所以示例可以在空的 RabbitMQ 上运行（拓扑）。

impl Handle<PriceChange, PriceChanged> for ChangePrice { fn handle( &self, change: &PriceChange, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<PriceChanged, HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(change.sku, change.price_cents, "price changed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fanout 交换机把每条消息复制到绑定它的每个队列，并忽略路由键。 change_price 以 PriceChanged 作为回复，店面和搜索索引各得到一份副本。 绑定的路由键为空，因为这个交换机不读取路由键。 新增一个价格变动的读者，只是多一个绑定到 prices 的队列；发布者不需要改动。

let mut attributes = HeaderMap::new(); attributes.insert("region", order.region.clone()); attributes.insert("tier", order.tier.clone()); let sent = outs .get(DefaultSlot) .message(&shipment) .with_headers(attributes) .publish() .await; sent.map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()) } } /// The binding arguments: how to match, then the headers matched on. fn gold_in_eu(x_match: &str) -> FieldTable { let mut arguments = FieldTable::default(); arguments.insert("x-match".into(), AMQPValue::LongString(x_match.into())); arguments.insert("region".into(), AMQPValue::LongString("eu".into())); arguments.insert("tier".into(), AMQPValue::LongString("gold".into())); arguments } /// Gold shipments in the EU: both headers have to match. struct BookExpress; impl Handle<Shipment> for BookExpress { fn handle( &self, shipment: &Shipment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(shipment.order_id, "express courier booked"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// Shipments that are gold or in the EU: one header is enough. struct Insure; impl Handle<Shipment> for Insure { fn handle( &self, shipment: &Shipment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(shipment.order_id, "shipment insured"); ready(Ok(())) } } headers 交换机按消息头而不是路由键来路由。 bind_with 为绑定指定参数：要匹配的消息头，以及 x-match，它规定其中多少个必须匹配。 取 all 时，消息必须匹配全部消息头；取 any 时，匹配一个就够了。 ship_order 用 with_headers 为每次发货设置 region 和 tier。 欧盟的 gold 级发货到达两个队列，欧盟的 silver 级发货只到达保险队列，美国的 silver 级发货哪个队列也不到达。 普通的 bind 用于按路由键路由的交换机。 在 headers 交换机上，它建立的绑定没有要匹配的消息头，而对空集合取 all 对每条消息都成立。 FieldTable 和 AMQPValue 来自 lapin，由 prelude 重新导出。

plugin-consistent-hash feature 加入 RabbitExchange::consistent_hash，即 RabbitMQ 一致性哈希插件提供的交换机类型。 它按路由键的哈希把一个消息流分散到多个队列，每个队列以自己的权重作为路由键进行绑定。 路由键相同的消息总是到达同一个队列。 插件必须在服务器上启用，路由也只在服务器上发生，所以它的测试针对真实的 RabbitMQ 运行。
示例文件中的测试发布一个订单、一次价格变动和三个已支付订单，并检查每条消息到达了哪些队列。 进程内 RabbitMQ 按描述符声明的同一组绑定，通过默认、direct、topic、fanout 和 headers 交换机进行路由。 测试 RabbitMQ 服务讲解了测试套件。
本指南让一个服务通过 RabbitMQ 调用另一个服务，并等待回复。 订单服务在接受订单之前，先询问库存服务某件商品是否有货。 调用经由 RabbitMQ 的 direct reply-to 进行：不需要声明回复队列，也不需要手工维护一张待处理调用表。

An RPC reply goes where the request asked, so the type names no /// destination. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] struct Stock { sku: String, available: bool, } #[subscriber("inventory.check", reply("inventory.check.unanswered"))] async fn check_stock(request: &CheckStock) -> Stock { tracing::info!(request.sku, request.quantity, "stock checked"); Stock { sku: request.sku.clone(), available: request.quantity <= 10, } } /// The inventory service's routes: each reply goes to the requester's own address. fn inventory() -> Router<LapinBroker, impl RouterDef<LapinBroker>> { Router::new() .include(check_stock) .out_reply(Publish::default()) .transform(DirectReplyTo) .build() } src/main.rs /// The stock of one SKU. An RPC reply goes where the request asked, so the type names no /// destination. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Stock { sku: String, available: bool, } struct Check; impl Handle<CheckStock, Stock> for Check { fn handle( &self, request: &CheckStock, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Stock, HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(request.sku, request.quantity, "stock checked"); ready(Ok(Stock { sku: request.sku.clone(), available: request.quantity <= 10, })) } } /// The inventory service's routes: each reply goes to the requester's own address. fn inventory() -> Router<LapinBroker, impl RouterDef<LapinBroker>> { Router::new() .include( subscriber("inventory.check", Check) .reply() .to("inventory.check.unanswered") .build(), ) .out_reply(Publish::default()) .transform(DirectReplyTo) .build() } 库存服务用一个返回回复的普通处理器作答。 回复发布者上的 DirectReplyTo 把每条回复发送到请求在其 reply-to 属性中指定的地址，并把请求的 correlation-id 复制到回复上。 Stock 没有指定目的地，因为每条回复都发往其请求要求的地方。 reply("inventory.check.unanswered") 中的名字，是回复没有 reply-to 的请求时所用的地址，也是服务的 AsyncAPI 文档所报告的地址。 这些路由是一个 Router，所以库存服务在自己的应用里用 b.include_router(inventory()) 挂载它们。 示例在一个进程里运行两个服务，并挂载两个路由器。

RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include_router(orders()); b.include_router(inventory()); }) } src/main.rs /// How long an order waits for the inventory service. const RPC_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2); /// How long an order waits before it asks again when the inventory service did not answer. const RETRY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Order { id: u64, sku: String, quantity: u32, } /// Asks the inventory service and waits for its answer. async fn ask_stock( inventory: &impl RequestReply, order: &Order, ) -> Result<Stock, Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>> { let request = JsonCodec.encode(&CheckStock { sku: order.sku.clone(), quantity: order.quantity, })?; let reply = inventory .request( OutgoingMessage::new("inventory.check", request.as_ref()), RPC_TIMEOUT, ) .await?; Ok(JsonCodec.decode(reply.payload())?) } struct PlaceOrder; impl<Inventory> Handle<Order, (), Outs<(Inventory,)>> for PlaceOrder where Inventory: OutEntry<DefaultSlot, Wire: RequestReply>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(Inventory,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { match ask_stock(outs.get(DefaultSlot), order).await { Ok(stock) if stock.available => { tracing::info!(order.id, "order accepted"); Ok(()) } Ok(_) => { tracing::warn!(order.id, "order rejected, out of stock"); Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()) } Err(err) => { tracing::warn!(order.id, %err, "inventory unavailable, asking again later"); Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RETRY)) } } } } /// The orders service's routes: the requester is a policy, paired with the connection at startup. fn orders() -> Router<LapinBroker, impl RouterDef<LapinBroker>> { Router::new() .include(subscriber("orders", PlaceOrder).build()) .out(DefaultSlot, Request::default()) .build() } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); // The example runs both services in one process; each service mounts its own router. RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include_router(orders()); b.include_router(inventory()); }) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } place_order 把它的槽位约束为 Out<impl RequestReply>，挂载点为它配上 Request 策略，即 LapinRequest。 每个请求带着路由键 inventory.check 发往默认交换机，所以它到达同名的队列。 请求的 reply-to 设为 RabbitMQ 的 amq.rabbitmq.reply-to，并带有一个新生成的 correlation-id。 id 相同的回复完成这次调用；id 不同的回复被丢弃。 这里的请求和回复都是字节，所以 ask_stock 用 JsonCodec 对它们编码和解码。 RPC_TIMEOUT 限定等待时间。 没有人及时应答时，调用返回 AmqpError::RequestTimeout 错误。 这时 place_order 用 retry_after 要求 30 秒后再投递这个订单，而不是去猜测库存。 商品缺货是业务上的答复，所以订单被丢弃。 这个策略接受发布所用的设置：exchange、priority 和 expiration。 请求默认是非持久化的：超时之后没人再等它，所以它在重启后存活下来也没有意义。 persistent(true) 让它持久化。

direct reply-to 是至多一次的。 回复地址存在于请求方位于某个 RabbitMQ 节点上的信道里，没有任何东西被持久地排入队列。 信道关闭时仍在途中的回复会丢失，调用方看到的是超时。 请求本身是普通队列里的一条普通消息：库存服务停机时，它在 inventory.check 中等待，可能在调用方放弃之后才得到应答。 所以库存查询可以安全地重复：应答两次不会改变任何东西。 请求方在自己的信道上读取回复，这个信道由它的第一个请求打开。
双方说的都是普通的 AMQP 0.9.1。 用其他客户端编写的应答方消费请求队列，把回复发布到默认交换机，路由键取自 reply-to，并复制 correlation-id。 带 DirectReplyTo 的 RustStream 应答方也以同样的方式回复用其他客户端编写的请求方。

documents.t: 进程内 RabbitMQ 属于连接它的那个应用，所以请求方和应答方必须运行在同一个应用里才能通信。 测试启动示例中挂载了两个路由器的应用，检查有货的订单被接受、缺货的订单被丢弃。 第三个测试在暂停的时钟上只挂载订单路由器：没有人应答，请求超时，订单稍后再次询问。 进程内 RabbitMQ 像服务器一样为每个请求分配自己的回复地址，并按关联 id 匹配回复。 测试 RabbitMQ 服务讲解了测试套件。

测试用 TestApp 运行服务自己的应用，连接的是进程内 RabbitMQ 或者运行中的服务器。 被测服务负责银行卡扣款。 付款到达 card-payments 队列，处理器在 card-receipts 上以一张收据作为回复。 没有金额的付款被丢弃。 超出银行即时限额的付款会被暂缓：处理器用 retry_after 要求一分钟后再投递它。 经过三次投递后，付款进入 card-payments.review。 应用由 service(broker) 构建，所以测试可以选择 Broker，而 main 使用生产环境的 Broker。 测试需要在 [dev-dependencies] 中启用 ruststream-lapin 的 testing feature。

let tb = TestApp::start(service(broker)).await?; let held = Payment { id: 3, amount_cents: 250_000, }; tb.broker::<LapinBroker>().message(&held).publish().await?; tb.broker::<LapinBroker>() .subscriber("card-payments") .assert_called_once() .settled(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(HOLD)); // The service holds the copy and publishes it back to the queue after `HOLD`. tb.advance(HOLD).await?; tb.broker::<LapinBroker>() .published::<Payment>("card-payments") .assert_called(2) .with(&held) .with_header(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER, "1"); // The third delivery is the last one: it goes to the review queue as it arrived. tb.advance(HOLD).await?; assert_eq!( tb.broker::<LapinBroker>() .subscriber("card-payments") .outcomes(), [Outcome::Nack, Outcome::Nack, Outcome::Nack], ); tb.broker::<LapinBroker>() .published::<Payment>("card-payments.review") .assert_called_once() .with(&held); tb.shutdown().await?; Ok(()) } src/main.rs #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)] async fn a_payment_the_bank_keeps_holding_goes_to_review() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let broker = LapinBroker::new("amqp://localhost:5672").declare_topology(true); let tb = TestApp::start(service(broker)).await?; let held = Payment { id: 3, amount_cents: 250_000, }; tb.broker::<LapinBroker>().message(&held).publish().await?; tb.broker::<LapinBroker>() .subscriber("card-payments") .assert_called_once() .settled(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(HOLD)); // The service holds the copy and publishes it back to the queue after `HOLD`. tb.advance(HOLD).await?; tb.broker::<LapinBroker>() .published::<Payment>("card-payments") .assert_called(2) .with(&held) .with_header(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER, "1"); // The third delivery is the last one: it goes to the review queue as it arrived. tb.advance(HOLD).await?; assert_eq!( tb.broker::<LapinBroker>() .subscriber("card-payments") .outcomes(), [Outcome::Nack, Outcome::Nack, Outcome::Nack], ); tb.broker::<LapinBroker>() .published::<Payment>("card-payments.review") .assert_called_once() .with(&held); tb.shutdown().await?; Ok(()) } 测试从暂停的时钟开始，advance 把时钟向前拨。 一分钟的 HOLD 不花任何时间。 队列没有 delay，所以服务持有副本，延迟结束时把它发布回 card-payments。 副本在消息头中带着重试次数，published 把它显示在测试自己发布的消息旁边。 第三次投递是挂载点允许的最后一次，所以付款按到达时的样子进入 card-payments.review。 每次被暂缓的投递都记录为 Outcome::Nack。

进程内 RabbitMQ 读取 Broker 的设置和各路由的描述符，与服务器看到的是同一份。 declare_topology 决定订阅是否声明自己的队列，与在服务器上一样。 它模拟的是 RabbitMQ，而不是一个通用队列： 默认、direct、topic、fanout 和 headers 交换机按描述符声明的绑定进行路由。 竞争消费者共享一个队列，重新入队的消息再次经过这个队列。 没有人消费时，队列保留到达它的消息；关闭的消费者把它取走而未结算的消息交还。 仲裁队列统计投递次数，并把用尽次数的消息经由其路线转为死信。 等待队列释放延迟副本，direct reply-to 为每个请求分配它自己的地址。 事务在提交之前不可见。 服务器拒绝的，它也拒绝：协议无法承载的名字或消息头、超过 16 MiB 的消息体、非排他的非持久队列、默认交换机上的绑定、以不同设置再次声明的队列、带优先级的仲裁队列。 在连接关闭之后结算的投递会报告信道已关闭。 只有服务器才具备的东西需要服务器来测试：预取窗口、发布者确认、信道事务的原子性、插件交换机、两个连接共享的队列，以及服务不声明就期望找到的队列。
